messages:

To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: MedSync Security <security@medsync.io>
Date: 2028-04-21T09:13:00-07:00
Subject: Getting started — Private deployment intake for MedSync

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for taking this on. We're ready to kick off the private deployment intake for MedSync (tenant id: MS-7420). Attached is a preliminary inventory (tenant-access-matrix.xlsx) and a high-level network sketch (medsync-network-diagram.png).

Immediate asks from our side:
- Confirm Redwood's required egress IP ranges for firewall allowlist.
- Clarify what service account / IAM roles you need from us for provisioning.
- KMS/keys approach: we plan to use our existing AWS KMS but need to know if Redwood needs key wrap or another flow.

Desired timeline: non-prod connectivity validated within 2 weeks, production cutover in ~6 weeks.

Can we schedule a 45m technical intake tomorrow or Friday? Prefer 11:00–14:00 PT.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Platform, MedSync

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Getting started — Private deployment intake for MedSync

Hi Sanjay — welcome, and thanks for the artifacts. I put Ben (network onboarding), Marissa (ops/runbook), and Grace (customer success) on thread so we can coordinate.

Quick answers up front:
- We'll provide a single egress CIDR block (preferred) and a fallback list of NAT IPs for the Dedicated gateway. Ben, see note below for exact ranges.
- For provisioning we prefer a Redwood-managed service account with scoped roles; if you must create the SA in your org we can accept a cross-account role with the minimal set (describe in checklist).
- KMS: Redwood supports both customer-managed KMS (we integrate via cross-account grant) and Redwood-managed keys. If you want to keep keys in your KMS, we'll need a short-term decrypt grant for image bootstrap and a long-term key policy as discussed below.

Attached is our onboarding checklist (redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf) — it's the short version, includes the gating items we'll validate in the intake call. Please review before the meeting.

Proposed next steps (intake call):
1) 30m technical walk (network, IAM, KMS) — align on IPs and routing.
2) 15m runbook/governance review (CS + Ops).
3) Agree on action items and owner for each gating item.

We can do tomorrow 11:30 PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and an agenda.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
--
attachment: redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medsync.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-21T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Getting started — Private deployment intake for MedSync

Thanks Kim / Sanjay — adding a few technical details for the firewall and network gating so MedSync can validate with their networking team before the call.

Network gating checklist (high level):
- Required: outbound NAT IPs (we'll provide a /28 preferred, or five static IPs).
- Required: TCP 443 outbound to api.redwood-inference.com and to our telemetry endpoints (will list IPs in follow-up).
- Required: Bi-directional TLS from your control-plane jump host to our provisioning endpoint (port 8443).
- Optional/Recommended: VPC peering for high-throughput private lane (if you want direct L2-like performance we can discuss).

Service accounts / IAM:
- Minimum permissions if you create roles in your cloud: (1) KMS: Encrypt/Decrypt for the customer key; (2) S3/GCS: PutObject/GetObject for model artifacts (scoped bucket only); (3) EC2/ECS: Describe/Attach for bootstrap ops (if relevant).

I attached a quick network diagram with suggested CIDR allocations and NAT IP examples (medsync-network-diagram.png).

I'll follow up after intake with concrete egress IPs and a short JSON snippet you can paste into your firewall config.

-ben
Ben Carter
Technical Onboarding, Redwood Dedicated

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Adding ops perspective and a short excerpt from the runbook we'll validate during intake. Karthik is copied for runtime connectivity patterns.

Runbook excerpt / validation gates we will check on the intake call:
- Environment inventory: list of subnets, CIDRs, and NAT ranges (we need exact CIDR for each env).
- Service account ownership: who rotates keys / who is primary contact for emergency ACL changes.
- KMS flow: test key wrap/unwrap in staging and produce an evidence PDF for audit (SOC readiness).
- Telemetry: where to send metrics and logs, retention window, and sampling rate.

Please confirm who owns the change window for production egress allowlist updates — MedSync or a 3rd party? That determines whether we need an on-call approval flow.

Attached: redwood-onprem-checklist.pdf (snippets embedded) — I'll paste the minimal acceptance criteria in the intake call agenda.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Deployment Operations, Redwood

Thanks everyone — appointment confirmed for 2028-04-25 11:30 PT. A few quick answers to get us started so the call is productive:

- Change window ownership: MedSync will own production firewall changes; we'll provide the change ticket and expected maintenance window.
- KMS: We're happy to create a cross-account role and grant to Redwood. We'll run the staging unwrap test on Wednesday and share evidence.
- Service account: we'll create an IAM role with the permissions Ben listed and share ARNs by end of day tomorrow.

We've attached the requested inventory and flagged the CIDR that corresponds to our staging environment in tenant-access-matrix.xlsx. We'll also upload the firewall change draft to the shared drive.

Look forward to the call — agenda request: please include a short smoke test checklist for the non-prod validation so the CS team can sign off during the call.

Best,
Priya Menon
